name: swipe-deck
title: Swipe deck
description: A stack of cards you fling away with a flick. Cards tilt with your finger, the next one rises to meet you, and the deck settles with spring physics.
interaction: Drag the top card sideways and release past the threshold, or flick it, to send it away. Release early and it springs back. The two round buttons swipe without dragging.
accessibility: The top card exposes named accessibility actions for both directions, and the buttons below are labeled native buttons. Cards beneath the top card are hidden from VoiceOver. Reduce Motion removes the tilt and fling travel.
integration: Bind an array of Identifiable items. The first item is the top card. The deck removes a card from the binding after it leaves, then calls onSwipe with its direction. Insert items at the front to undo. Give the deck a frame with enough height for cards and controls.
uikitUsage:
let deck = HugsySwipeDeckViewController(items: cards) { card in
  CardView(card: card)
}
deck.didSwipe = { card, direction in
  print(card.id, direction)
}
addChild(deck)
view.addSubview(deck.view)
deck.didMove(toParent: self)

name: parallax-carousel
title: Parallax carousel
description: A paging carousel where cards tilt in 3D, scale into focus, and slide their artwork at a different speed than the card itself.
interaction: Swipe horizontally. Cards snap into place, neighbors peek from both edges, and the artwork inside each card drifts against the scroll. Tap an indicator to jump to a card.
accessibility: Uses a native ScrollView, so VoiceOver and keyboard scrolling work normally. Each indicator is a labeled button that announces its position. Reduce Motion removes the 3D tilt and parallax drift while keeping paging.
integration: Supply Identifiable items, a selection binding, and a content builder. Content is drawn slightly wider than the card so it has room to drift, so avoid placing text near the side edges. Give the carousel a fixed height.
usage:
@State private var selection: Place.ID?

HugsyParallaxCarousel(items: places, selection: $selection) { place in
  Image(place.photo)
    .resizable()
    .scaledToFill()
}
.frame(height: 460)
uikitUsage:
let carousel = HugsyParallaxCarouselViewController(items: places) { place in
  UIImageView(image: UIImage(named: place.photo))
}
carousel.didSelect = { id in
  print("Selected", id as Any)
}
addChild(carousel)
view.addSubview(carousel.view)
carousel.didMove(toParent: self)

name: morphing-capsule
title: Morphing capsule
description: A floating black capsule that stretches between a compact pill, a wide alert, and an expanded panel, blurring its content between shapes.
interaction: Tap the capsule to expand it and tap again to collapse. Pull it downward to expand and push it upward to collapse. It rubber-bands as you drag.
accessibility: The capsule announces its phase and acts as a button while collapsed. The Escape gesture collapses it. Content cross-fades instead of blurring when Reduce Motion is on, and the shape changes without spring travel.
integration: Bind a HugsyCapsulePhase and return content for each phase. Content is rendered on black with a dark color scheme. Place it at the top of your screen, below the status bar. Adjust the three sizes to fit your content.
uikitUsage:
let capsule = HugsyMorphingCapsuleViewController { phase in
  PhaseView(phase: phase)
}
capsule.didChangePhase = { phase in
  print(phase)
}
capsule.phase = .alert

name: expanding-cards
title: Expanding cards
description: Cards that open into an immersive detail view, with shared geometry and a drag-to-dismiss gesture.
interaction: Tap a card to open its details. Drag downward to dismiss, or use the close button.
accessibility: Native buttons expose card actions. Expanded content hides the underlying cards from VoiceOver. A labeled close button and Escape accessibility action provide alternatives to dragging. Reduce Motion removes spring interpolation.
integration: Supply Identifiable items and one content builder. The builder receives the item and its expanded state. Keep card IDs stable and unique. Place the component in a container with enough vertical room for the expanded content. It is an inline expanding surface, not a system modal sheet.
uikitUsage:
let cards = HugsyExpandingCardsViewController(items: stories) { story, expanded in
  StoryView(story: story, expanded: expanded)
}
cards.didSelect = { id in
  print("Open", id as Any)
}
addChild(cards)
view.addSubview(cards.view)
cards.didMove(toParent: self)

name: radial-menu
title: Radial menu
description: A floating action menu with a rotating trigger, staggered spring entrances, and an arc of reachable actions.
interaction: Open the action menu, then choose an action. The actions spring outward in sequence and collapse after selection.
accessibility: Every action is a labeled native button. Collapsed actions are removed from hit testing and accessibility. The trigger announces expanded or collapsed state. Reduce Motion removes travel interpolation and trigger rotation.
integration: Supply stable, unique action IDs and main-actor closures. Use three or four actions to keep targets separated. Reserve the component's full width and height in the layout. Actions close the menu before running their closures.

name: stacked-cards
title: Stacked cards
description: Cards stacked in a pile you cycle. Drag the front card up or down past the threshold to send it to the back, and the next card steps forward.
interaction: Drag the front card up or down past the threshold to send it to the back, and the next card becomes the front.
accessibility: The front card exposes a named action to send the card to the back. Cards under the front card are hidden from VoiceOver. Reduce Motion relocates cards instantly and removes the rotation.
integration: Bind an array of Identifiable items; the first item is the front card. Cycling moves the front item to the end of the binding and calls onCycle. Give the component a frame with enough height for cardHeight.
uikitUsage:
let stack = HugsyStackedCardsViewController(items: cards) { card in
  CardView(card: card)
}
stack.didCycle = { card in
  print(card.id)
}
addChild(stack)
view.addSubview(stack.view)
stack.didMove(toParent: self)

name: uikit-bridge
title: UIKit bridge
description: Shared helpers that host Hugsy components inside UIKit view controllers and display your own UIViews inside them.
interaction: Not interactive on its own. Each component's view controller uses it to embed SwiftUI and to wrap your UIViews.
accessibility: Hosted SwiftUI keeps its native accessibility tree. UIViews you supply keep their own accessibility configuration.
integration: Installed automatically with any component's UIKit adapter. HugsyUIViewBox wraps a UIView for use in SwiftUI. Views passed to adapters are cached per item, so return a fresh view for each item and configure it fully.
